title: 2023 AMC 12B Problem 6
statement:
When the roots of the polynomial

\[ \begin{gathered} P(x)=(x-1)^1(x-2)^2 \\ {}\cdot (x-3)^3\cdots \\ {}\cdot (x-10)^{10} \end{gathered} \]

are removed from the number line, what remains is the union of \(11\) disjoint open intervals. On how many of these intervals is \(P(x)\) positive?

solutions.text:
The exponent of the factor \((x-k)\) is \(k,\) so the sign of \(P\) changes at \(x=k\) only when \(k\) is odd, i.e. at \(1,3,5,7,9.\) For \(x\gt 10\) every factor is positive, so \(P\gt 0.\) Sweeping left and flipping at each odd root, the positive intervals are \((10,\infty),\) \((9,10),\) \((6,7),\) \((5,6),\) \((2,3),\) and \((1,2)\) — six intervals in all.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The sign of \(P(x)\) flips at a root only when that root’s exponent is odd
For \(x\gt 10\) the value is positive; move left, flipping sign only at the odd roots \(1,3,5,7,9\)
